questions.question: A solid has 6 square faces. What is it?
questions.explain: A cube has 6 faces and every one is a square. A rectangular prism has rectangles, a cylinder has round faces, and a sphere has no flat faces at all.

questions.question: A solid has 2 round faces and 1 curved face. What is it?
questions.explain: A cylinder has 2 round faces (top and bottom) and 1 curved side. A cone has only 1 round face, and cubes and rectangular prisms have only flat faces.

questions.question: A solid has no flat faces at all. It is perfectly round. What is it?
questions.explain: A sphere is all curved with no flat faces. A cylinder has 2 flat faces, a cone has 1, and a cube has 6.

questions.question: A solid has 1 round face and 1 curved face. It comes to a point at the top. What is it?
questions.explain: A cone has 1 round face at the bottom, 1 curved side, and a pointy top. A cylinder has 2 round faces, a sphere has no flat faces, and a cube has square faces.

questions.question: Sam is wrapping a birthday gift. His box has 6 flat faces. Every face is a rectangle. The box is not a cube. What shape is the box?
questions.explain: A rectangular prism has 6 flat rectangular faces. A cube has square faces, a cylinder has round faces, and a cone has a round face plus a curved side.

questions.question: Tom says: I have a solid with 5 square faces. It must be a cube. What did Tom get wrong?
options: A cube has 7 square faces, not 5.
A cube has 6 square faces, not 5.
A cube has 5 faces, but they are rectangles.
A cube has round faces, not square ones.
questions.explain: A cube always has 6 square faces. Tom counted 5, which is one too few. The faces of a cube are squares, not rectangles or round shapes.

questions.question: Nina cuts out a net with 6 flat pieces: 4 rectangles and 2 squares. She folds it into a solid. What 3D solid does she make?
questions.explain: A rectangular prism can have 4 rectangle faces and 2 square faces. A cube needs all 6 faces to be squares. A cylinder and a cone need round faces in their nets.

questions.question: Rosa has a net with 2 circles and 1 rectangle. She folds it up into a solid. She then counts the flat faces on her finished solid. How many flat faces does her solid have?
questions.explain: Two circles and one rectangle make a cylinder. A cylinder has exactly 2 flat faces (the two circles). The rectangle wraps around to become the curved side, not a flat face.

questions.question: Ava has a net with 6 flat pieces. 4 pieces are rectangles. The other 2 pieces are the same shape. When she folds it, the solid is NOT a cube. What shape are the 2 matching pieces?
questions.explain: A rectangular prism that is not a cube can have 4 rectangle faces and 2 square faces. Circles belong to cylinders, ovals are not flat faces of any standard solid, and triangles would make a pyramid, not a rectangular prism.

questions.question: Maya is making a paper cylinder to hold pencils. It needs a flat top and a flat bottom. Which pieces should Maya cut?
questions.explain: A cylinder has 2 flat faces that are circles, plus 1 curved piece that opens up flat as a rectangle. The flat faces are circles, never squares.

questions.question: Leo builds a straw skeleton in art class. It has 2 triangle faces and 3 rectangle faces. What solid did Leo build?
questions.explain: Count the face shapes: 2 triangles and 3 rectangles make 5 faces, so it is a triangular prism. A rectangular prism would need 6 rectangle faces instead.

questions.question: Nora is making a paper cone for a craft fair. The bottom must be closed. Which pieces should Nora cut?
questions.explain: A cone has only 1 flat face, and that face is a circle. The curved piece wraps around it up to a point, so a triangle is not one of the pieces.

questions.question: Ravi is folding paper to make a cube for a board game. Ravi has cut 5 equal squares so far. How many more squares are needed?
questions.explain: A cube is closed by 6 square faces, so 5 squares leave one hole open and 1 more square is needed. Five squares can never fold into a closed cube.
